tagline: The global average looks flat. A few regions are not.
challenge: Be An Earth System Trend Detective! (NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026)

dataset.name: GLDAS-2.1 Noah Land Surface Model L4 monthly 0.25 x 0.25 degree

aggregate.method: OLS slope; p = max(AR(1)-parametric SE with bias-corrected rho [t(n-k)], annual-mean OLS with AR(1) n_eff [Santer 2000]) (intersection-union)

headline.weights: true land area of valid cells (area_km2__Rainf_f_tavg)

methods.trend: OLS slope; p = max(AR(1)-parametric SE with bias-corrected rho [t(n-k)], annual-mean OLS with AR(1) n_eff [Santer 2000]) (intersection-union)
methods.spatial: local Moran's I (LISA) on trend_slope_pct, 9,999 conditional permutations, BH-FDR; queen weights with dateline wrap; kNN and Getis-Ord Gi* robustness
methods.regions: connected (8-neighbour, dateline-aware) tiles labelled trend_slope_pct HH/LL by LISA AND BH-significant (q<0.05) with the matching sign; >= 5 tiles

caveats: GLDAS-2.1 precipitation is model forcing derived from GPCP; it is not an independent rain-gauge record.
Trends are statistical over 2000-2025; they shrink in shorter windows and do not identify causes.
Tile shares are after false-discovery correction; individual tiles can still be false positives.

retraction.text: Soil water was the original headline: a 26-year global decline. Paradox Earth's own checks showed it is mostly two level shifts that follow documented changes in the radiation data driving the GLDAS model (a step in 2010-08 and a degraded period from 2024-07; GES DISC README_GLDAS2). Within the single consistent period 2012-01 to 2024-06 the global decline is not significant, so the trend was withdrawn and soil water is analysed only inside that window.
